## Upgrade

- **Migration 040.** Run `hot db migrate` with the 3.0.10 CLI. It adds a partial index on `blob_ref` for the refs that hold spilled call payloads. On Postgres it is built concurrently, so writes don't wait. See [Upgrading from 3.0.9 to 3.0.10](/docs/migrations#upgrading-from-3-0-9-to-3-0-10).
- **`hot.profile.set` no longer selects a profile.** Use `hot.set.profile`. A project that still selects its profile with the old key gets `local-dev`.
- **Bytecode caches are rebuilt once** after the upgrade.

## Features

Compiled code is faster across the board. Times below are against 3.0.9 on the repository's benchmarks:

| | 3.0.9 | 3.0.10 |
|---|---|---|
| `word-count(50000)` | 191 ms | 19 ms |
| `json-benchmark(1000)` | 1.71 ms | 0.96 ms |
| `json-api-roundtrip(1500)` | 13.6 ms | 8.4 ms |
| `closure-capture(10000)` | 1.31 ms | 0.71 ms |
| `nested-hof(100)` | 2.24 ms | 1.37 ms |
| `fib-recursive(25)` | 1.07 ms | 0.74 ms |
| `fn-as-value(10000)` | 9.2 ms | 6.6 ms |
| `records-reshape(2000)` | 9.5 ms | 7.1 ms |
| `hot run` of hello world | 50 ms | 33 ms |

- **Compiled code writes collections in place.** A compiled `reduce` with `assoc`, `merge`, `concat` or a leading spread, and a call that hands a dead value to another function, no longer copy the collection at each step. Counting into a Map that has stopped growing, and reading the accumulator before writing it, were still copying on 3.0.9. Builders now stay compiled at every size; 3.0.9 sent them to the interpreter past 1,024 items.
- **`to-json` and `from-json` work straight from and to values,** without an intermediate tree. Output is unchanged.
- **Calls are cheaper.**
  - A loop such as `map` or `reduce` calls its compiled callback directly, without looking it up again for each item.
  - A function held in a value is called without resolving it or checking its arguments twice.
  - Compiled calls carry the stack limit with them, and check for cancellation once per 1,024 calls or loop iterations instead of at each one.
- **Map literals are built at their full size** in one step.
- **Map keys hash with aHash,** not SipHash. Maps keep insertion order as before.
- **Startup is about 17 ms shorter.** A `hot.hot` made only of settings, and `::hot::env/get` calls with literal arguments, is read directly instead of running hot-std first. Every file `hot init` writes qualifies. Any other configuration runs as before.
- **Smaller costs:**
  - Template strings write Str and Int parts directly.
  - `reduce(range(n), …)` streams the range when nothing else reads it.
  - Call frames and value drops do less work.

## Fixes

- **Call retention frees spilled call payloads.** Deleting old calls left the refs to their spilled arguments and return values active, so blob GC never reclaimed them, and the blob store grew without bound under heavy call traffic. The daily pass's single `UPDATE` hit the statement timeout once a few million refs had built up, and local-dev startup retention never released them at all. Retention now releases them in batches of 10,000. An install with a backlog drains it on the first daily pass after the upgrade, and blob GC frees the objects after its usual grace period.

## Behaviour changes

- **`hot.profile.set` is removed.** `hot.set.profile` is the only profile selector, and `hot.profile.set` is now a profile named `set`, like any other key under `hot.profile`.
- **The 1,024-item limit on compiled builders is gone.** Builders no longer switch to the interpreter as they grow.
